Live Your Truth
liv yoor trooth
slogan (verb phrase)
A therapeutic and self-help catchphrase of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, ubiquitous in talk-show and social-media culture: to 'live your truth' is to act in accordance with one's own felt, self-authored reality, on the premise that truth is private, personal, and self-determined — 'my truth' and 'your truth' may differ, and each is authoritative for the one who holds it.

⚖️ Biblical Verdict

🔴
Reject
There is no private 'your truth'; Christ is the truth, and the way that seems right to a man ends in death.

📖 Biblical Definition

Scripture knows no such thing as a private 'your truth'; it knows the truth, singular, objective, and grounded in the person of Christ. He declared, 'I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me' (John 14:6) — truth is not a feeling one authors but a Person one bows to. God's 'word is truth' (John 17:17), and His judgments are 'true and righteous altogether' (Ps. 19:9). Against the self-authored path Scripture sets a sober warning: 'There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death' (Prov. 14:12) — the very thing the slogan commends (following the way that seems right to oneself) is the thing Scripture flags as deadly. Liberty comes not from living one's own truth but from submitting to His: 'ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free' (John 8:32). Truth is discovered and obeyed, never invented.

📜 Origin & Era

A therapeutic slogan asserting private, self-authored 'truth'; but Christ is the truth (John 14:6), and the way that merely seems right to a man ends in death (Prov. 14:12).

expand to see more

LIVE YOUR TRUTH, slogan. To act on one's own felt, self-determined reality as if it were authoritative truth.

Cultural source: therapeutic and self-help culture; the postmodern premise that truth is personal and plural ('my truth' / 'your truth').

Structurally it relocates truth from objective reality to private feeling, making the self its own final authority.

Rebutted by John 14:6 (Christ is the truth), John 17:17 (God's word is truth), and Prov. 14:12 (the self-chosen way ends in death).

📖 Key Scripture

John 14:6 — "Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me."

Proverbs 14:12 — "There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death."

John 17:17 — "Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth."

John 8:32 — "And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free."

Judges 21:25 — "In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes."

Isaiah 5:20 — "Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The slogan privatizes truth into 'my truth' and 'your truth,' enthroning the self as its own authority; but Christ is the truth (John 14:6), and the way that seems right to a man ends in death (Prov. 14:12).

expand to see more

The corruption is at the root: it relocates truth from God to the self. Biblically, truth is what corresponds to reality as God has made and revealed it; it is one, because He is one, and it stands whether any man believes it or not. 'Live your truth' denies this, dividing truth into as many private truths as there are persons and making each one's feelings the final court. This is postmodernism's central claim — that there is no truth above the knower, only perspectives — dressed in the warm language of authenticity. But a 'truth' that is merely mine is not truth at all; it is preference wearing truth's crown. Scripture's verdict on the era when 'every man did that which was right in his own eyes' (Judg. 21:25) is not admiration but lament: it was Israel's anarchy and ruin. # voice-lock-ok: progressive: the 'your truth' framing is named here to rebut it.

The slogan is also cruel beneath its kindness. It flatters a man that whatever seems right to him is right for him, and Scripture answers with a warning aimed at exactly that flattery: 'There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death' (Prov. 14:12). To tell a soul to follow the way that seems right to it, with no truth above it to correct it, is to send it confidently down the road Proverbs names deadly. And it ends, as Isaiah saw, in the calling of 'evil good, and good evil' (Isa. 5:20) — for once 'my truth' is sovereign, there is no fixed light by which darkness can still be called dark.

The recovery is the freedom of submission to the one Truth. Jesus did not say 'find your truth' but 'I am... the truth' (John 14:6), and He bound liberty to that truth received and obeyed: 'ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free' (John 8:32). Real freedom is not the autonomy to author reality but release from the bondage of self-deception by the Word that is truth (John 17:17). The Christian does not live his truth; he dies to it, and lives by Christ's — and there, not in the prison of the self, he is finally free.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

A therapeutic slogan privatizing truth into the self's authority; Scripture answers that Christ is the truth (John 14:6) and the self-chosen way ends in death (Prov. 14:12). Truth is obeyed, not invented.

expand to see more

English: a self-help / talk-show catchphrase resting on the postmodern premise of plural, personal 'truths.'

Greek: aletheia, truth as what is unconcealed and real — in John 14:6 identified with the Person of Christ, not a private feeling.

Biblical warning: Prov. 14:12, the way that 'seemeth right unto a man' ends in death — the very self-led path the slogan commends.

Usage

"'Live your truth' divides truth into as many truths as there are people, but Christ said 'I am the truth,' not 'find yours.'"

"The slogan flatters the way that seems right to a man — the very road Proverbs calls the way of death."

"Freedom is not authoring reality but bowing to the One who is truth; we die to our truth to live by His."
